s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital facial asymmetry with abnormal lip movement
salient_findings: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
key_facts: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
Developmental milestones are appropriate for age
Normal magnetic resonance imaging of the temporal bones and internal auditory canals

raw.syndrome_frame: Congenital facial asymmetry with abnormal lip movement
salient_findings: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
key_facts: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
Developmental milestones are appropriate for age
Normal magnetic resonance imaging of the temporal bones and internal auditory canals

shortlist.label: Congenital Lower Lip Palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the specific symptom of right lower lip deviation

shortlist.label: Moebius Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to abnormal lip movement, although other facial movements are symmetric

shortlist.label: Hemifacial Microsomia
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of congenital facial asymmetry

shortlist.label: Facial Hemiatrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain facial asymmetry, although typically presents with progressive atrophy

shortlist.label: Congenital Facial Diplegia
shortlist.why_kept: Rare condition that could cause abnormal facial movement, including lip deviation

raw.rationale: The key fact that the right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying, with otherwise symmetric facial movement, is most consistent with Congenital Lower Lip Palsy.

rejected.label: Moebius Syndrome
rejected.why: Moebius Syndrome typically involves bilateral facial weakness and is often associated with other abnormalities, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Hemifacial Microsomia
rejected.why: Hemifacial Microsomia involves underdevelopment of one side of the face, which is not described in this patient.

rejected.label: Facial Hemiatrophy
rejected.why: Facial Hemiatrophy is a progressive condition that typically presents later in life and is not consistent with the congenital onset described.

rejected.label: Congenital Facial Diplegia
rejected.why: Congenital Facial Diplegia involves bilateral facial weakness, which is not consistent with the unilateral lower lip deviation described in this case.
